title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore overview
text: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is a set of services for deploying and operating AI agents at scale. It includes Runtime (serverless hosting with session isolation), Memory (short- and long-term memory), Gateway (turns APIs and Lambda functions into agent tools), Identity (inbound/outbound auth), Code Interpreter, Browser, Observability (OpenTelemetry traces and metrics in CloudWatch) and Evaluations (built-in and custom evaluators). It works with any framework such as Strands Agents, LangGraph or CrewAI and any model.

title: AgentCore Runtime
text: AgentCore Runtime hosts agents as containers (linux/arm64) pulled from Amazon ECR, or as direct code deployments from S3. The container must listen on port 8080 and expose POST /invocations and GET /ping. Each runtime session runs in an isolated microVM; sessions can last up to 8 hours and are billed on active CPU and memory consumption.

title: AgentCore Memory
text: AgentCore Memory stores raw conversation events (short-term memory) and asynchronously extracts long-term memory records using strategies: semantic (facts), summary (per-session summaries), user preference, and episodic. Records are organised into namespaces such as /preferences/{actorId}/ and retrieved with semantic search.

title: AgentCore Observability
text: AgentCore Observability emits OpenTelemetry-compatible traces, spans and metrics to Amazon CloudWatch. It requires CloudWatch Transaction Search to be enabled once per account. The CloudWatch GenAI Observability dashboard shows sessions, traces, latency, token usage, error rates and tool calls. Agents instrument themselves with the AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry (ADOT).

title: AgentCore Evaluations
text: AgentCore Evaluations scores agent behaviour using trace data. Built-in evaluators include Builtin.Helpfulness, Builtin.Correctness, Builtin.Faithfulness, Builtin.GoalSuccessRate, Builtin.ToolSelectionAccuracy and Builtin.Harmfulness. Online evaluation continuously samples live traffic; on-demand evaluation scores specific sessions, optionally with ground-truth reference inputs such as expected responses or assertions.

title: Multi-agent patterns
text: Common multi-agent patterns are: agents-as-tools (an orchestrator calls specialist agents as tools), graph (a deterministic DAG of agents), swarm (agents hand off to each other autonomously) and workflow. The agents-as-tools pattern is the easiest to reason about and observe because the orchestrator owns control flow.

title: Serverless compute on AWS
text: AWS Lambda runs functions for up to 15 minutes with pay-per-request billing. AWS Fargate runs containers without managing servers. Serverless designs reduce operational overhead but require attention to cold starts, timeouts and concurrency limits.

title: Retrieval-augmented generation
text: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) grounds model answers in retrieved documents. A typical pipeline chunks documents, embeds them, stores vectors in a vector store, retrieves the top-k chunks for a query and passes them to the model with instructions to cite sources. Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases provide a managed RAG pipeline.
